tasks.title: Cell registry 1/5: registry module, management CLI, single grid module
tasks.notes: Part of the cell-registry epic (tickets 29-33, one new branch off main, one PR; do NOT use the bakeoff-r004 branch). DESIGN (agreed in grilling session): world data lives in the active world: registry/cells.json + registry/features.json, sparse (absent cell = empty), written ONLY through one registry module (atomic write, sorted keys); LLM reads only via a documented management command. Cell record: ground none|ghost|ghost+features|generated; trees bool; decor bool; marker up|none; hold reason|null. Derived, never stored: empty, DONE, current cell (= marker cell), a cell's features. DONE = ground generated + trees + decor + every registered feature in the cell built + no marker + no open OSM-coverage warnings. Feature record: id = build slug (matches site/builds/<name>.json), name, cells touched, status planned|in-progress|built (one status per feature). Invariants enforced in code (refused write raises error naming the rule, nothing changes): single marker; ghost+features only on ghost ground; trees/decor only on generated ground; rebuilding ground clears trees+decor; reopening a feature clears trees+decor in every cell it touches. Management CLI with clear docs: query (is feature X built, what is left in cell C, status), register feature (explicit list; helper proposes OSM candidates), hold set/clear, dismiss OSM warning with reason. GRID: one cellmath module owns cell size, bounds, cell->region mapping, ring order, parse_cell and the id format; delete the other definitions (world_frame.CELL/cell_of/cell_bounds/parse_cell, coverage.cell_of/cell_bbox, pass_mask.CELL_SIZE, site_stages.CELL_SHIFT, ground_sources.mc_tile_for_cell, ref_manifest.mc_tile_id, lidar_ghost use of CELL_SHIFT). Cell id is always the string 'tx,tz' (e.g. 48,-44); 'm44' spelling only inside file names. Origin cell and cell size move into the world's world-frame.json (remove hard-coded ORIGIN_CELL in cellmath.py and CENTRE in site_status.py). Tests for all invariants. Done 2026-10-21 on cell-registry-tickets: scripts/cell_registry.py + CLI; cellmath owns grid (size/origin from world-frame cell); invariant tests; callers delegate. World checkout: config/world-frame.json cell block + empty registry/.

tasks.title: Cell registry 2/5: make build commands update the registry automatically
tasks.notes: PRINCIPLE: the registry is updated by code as a side effect of build commands, not by LLM-followed rules. ground_layer/trees_layer/decor_layer set ground/trees/decor on a clean readback only. site_kit.apply: feature status in-progress on begin, built only on clean readback (zero mismatches; mismatches stay in-progress); cells touched overwritten from the real footprint. cell_marker raise/clear sets marker (marker no longer counts as work or as a STAGES entry). lidar_ghost keeps its state machine but writes only to the registry: ghost lay-down around the marker cell (default ring 2; ground none->ghost / ghost+features); real feature apply strips ghost features first (ghost+features -> ghost); real ground apply -> generated and drops ghost features; markers never count as real work. Every block-removing command clears the matching flags in the same step: mask_undo, strip_cell_above_ground, ghost supersede/strip, site_recover. A failed apply never sets flags. Feature specs stay in site/builds/<name>.json; *-cells.json ownership files stay as block-level evidence the registry points to (not a second status record). Per-run detail (readback, snapshot, structure/from/to) goes to the existing *-result.json / *-backup.json; masks stay under verification/site/masks. Tests per writer. Done 2026-10-21 on cell-registry-tickets: registry_hooks + site_kit.apply begin/clean, cell_marker raise/clear/adopt, mask_undo, strip_cell_above_ground, site_recover rollback, lidar_ghost feature strip demotion. Tests: test_registry_hooks + site_recover apply cases.

tasks.title: Cell registry 3/5: replace STAGES, QUEUE, handoff, sign-offs, holds, AERIAL-REVIEW, CURRENT-CELL; add next + issues; rewrite orchestrator
tasks.notes: DELETE: per-cell STAGES.json (all readers - cell_gaps, layers_done, requeue_plan, real_work_started, ground_done, site_status, site_pages, site_recover, lump_scan - read the registry instead); QUEUE.txt + Q-nnn ids + site_handoff queue writing/advance_to_next_cell + .handoff-pending.json + set_pending/clear_pending + the whole handoff system; COVERAGE-SIGNOFFS.jsonl and ALL sign-off code, rules, docs, tests (system runs unsupervised); CELL-HOLDS.jsonl (becomes cell hold field); AERIAL-REVIEW.txt and its code (site_handoff.py ~147-247); CURRENT-CELL.json and every other way of tracking the current cell (coverage.focus_cell, site_status centre, queue 'marker must be up' text); coverage.cell_rollup (COVERAGE.txt generated block now produced from the registry). KEEP/ADD: `next` registry command, read-only and deterministic (idempotent): open issues first, then next undone item. Cell choice: marker cell if not DONE, else nearest undone non-held cell to the configured origin ordered by distance then clockwise ring order from north (the build task raises the marker, next does not). Order inside a cell: ground, then features in registry order, then trees, then decor. ISSUES.txt = snagging backlog, one parsed line per issue with a registry target and reason, e.g. 'I-014  cell 48,-44 trees  <why>' / 'I-015  feature q001_university_road_42  <why>'; target is cell layer, feature id or whole cell; add-issue command reopens the target; auto-closes on clean rebuild and archives with date. Rewrite cell-orchestrator skill as a thin loop: run next, launch one subagent per task (a cell layer, a feature, or an issue), wait; a handoff is just a fresh session running next. Update human-confirm-fix and redo skills accordingly. DONE: registry next + ISSUES/add-issue/auto-close; cell_gaps/layers_done/ground_done/focus/lidar real_work/site_status marker from registry; QUEUE advance/cmd_next redirected; aerial-review + coverage signoffs retired as progress; orchestrator/redo/confirm-fix rewritten. tasks.title: Cell registry 4/5: repair cell, whole-world backup pair, logout gate, verify
tasks.notes: repair <cell>: back up ONLY the impacted region files (region holding the cell plus any region its features/trees/decor spill into, from *-cells.json footprints and masks) together with that cell's registry record; wipe only that cell's columns to air above bedrock; replay from the registry clipped to the cell bounds (ghost ground/features if ghost state, else ground, features in registry order, trees, decor; features from site/builds specs); re-raise marker if it was up; if any step fails, clear flags for that step and all later ones so next picks it up. 'undo repair' restores the region files and the saved registry record. Bake-off: wipe the WHOLE world each round, restore ONE whole-world backup paired with a whole-registry copy (no per-cell slices); update model_bakeoff.restore_ghost_step and region_backup. Raw region_backup restore of a partial snapshot is refused (error points at the proper undo/redo command) except via repair-undo and the full-world bake-off restore. LOGOUT GATE: every command that rewrites region files (repair, undo repair, bake-off wipe/restore, dryrun_reset) refuses without --confirm-logged-out, stops and plays the need-you sound asking the user to log out; second guard checks session.lock / a running server holding the save and refuses even with the flag. VERIFY (report only, exit non-zero on any error): invariants; marker rings vs registry (exactly the marked cell has a stripe ring); region files exist for cells with ground and no blocks in cells the registry calls empty; built features have ownership files and blocks still present; registered features have specs; OSM buildings no registered feature covers (warnings that block DONE until resolved or dismissed with a reason); leftover old-system files (STAGES, QUEUE, CURRENT-CELL, sign-offs). Hook verify into scripts/run_tests.py / dryrun_reset where sensible. DONE: logout_gate (--confirm-logged-out + session.lock/MCP refuse); region_backup kind partial/whole-world/repair + snap-world; raw restore refuses partial; registry_repair backup/undo/replay-plan/clear-flags; cell_registry repair|undo-repair|verify; model_bakeoff restore-ghost; dryrun_reset logout gate + post-reset verify. Partial: live feature/trees/decor replay still raises to manual CLI; full OSM/block verify and bake-off per-round wipe deferred toward #33.

tasks.title: ship_branch.py merge: tested branch into main, then clean up
tasks.notes: Part of the branch-gate policy (decided in grill, 2026-10-22): code is built on task/* branches and always ends merged. `scripts/ship_branch.py merge <branch>`: run scripts/run_tests.py on the branch tip; merge --no-ff (matches history); re-run the tests on main; delete the branch and its worktree. Any failure stops and reports, no auto-revert. Unit tests on throwaway git repos: green merge, failing tip, failing main after merge. Worker rule unchanged: workers leave the tracker alone. Merged via wave 61-65: ship_branch.py merge + tests on main (cf5a57a).

tasks.title: ship-branch skill: build, review, fix, merge loop
tasks.notes: Project skill under .claude/skills/. Builder session finishing a code change runs: tests, then a fresh-context read-only reviewer subagent on Sonnet at high effort, then a normal-tier fixer (default model, normal effort, same worktree) on blockers, re-review, up to 3 review rounds, then ship_branch.py merge. Tests failing before review go to the fixer and count toward the cap. If main moved, the fixer merges main into the branch; re-review only if the resolution touched more than conflict markers. Reviewer brief is fixed: branch diff vs main, CODING_STANDARDS.md, GLOSSARY.md, accepted ADRs, ticket text, test coverage; returns APPROVE or CHANGES with blocker/nit findings; never edits. Only blockers loop; nits become tracker follow-ups or are dropped if trivial. Ask the owner before using Opus or any other high-cost model; everything else is automatic. Opt-outs in the owner's words: 'no review'/'skip review' (build, test, merge) and 'leave on branch'/'don't merge' (stop after build, report branch; implies no review). A ticket may carry review: skip. Cap hit or any stop: leave the branch unmerged and play need-you. Check by running it on one trivial real change. Bootstrapping: #61-#63 themselves are built on task/* branches and merged by the orchestrator after a manual pass. Merged via wave 61-65: .claude/skills/ship-branch/SKILL.md on main.

Offers to merge tracker/docs-only strays; code strays are reported and wait for the owner's call (review-and-merge or delete). Never deletes or merges code on its own.
